title: Observational Reasoning
purpose: Seed observational-study reasoning so Lantern can select and interpret cohort, case-control, cross-sectional, longitudinal and natural/quasi-experimental evidence while explicitly tracking selection, confounding, temporality, missingness and causal limits.

concepts.definition: A study in which relevant exposures/conditions are observed rather than assigned by the investigator.
Observation of variables at one time/limited window, useful for prevalence/association but often weak for temporal direction.
A design following or reconstructing groups defined by exposure/characteristics to compare subsequent outcomes.
A cohort defined before future outcomes are observed and followed forward.
A cohort reconstructed from existing records where exposure/outcome events may already have occurred.
A design selecting cases with an outcome and controls without it, then comparing prior exposures/characteristics.
Repeated observation of units over time, enabling change/temporal-pattern analysis without automatically establishing causality.
Repeated measurements on the same units across time.
An external event/rule/process creates exposure variation that may approximate an intervention under defensible assumptions.
A design estimating intervention effects without randomized assignment using a structured comparison/identification strategy.
Systematic distortion arising when inclusion/retention/analysis selection is related to variables relevant to the inference.
Distortion of an exposure-outcome association by common causes or related structures not appropriately handled.
Outcome or pre-outcome processes influence the supposed exposure/predictor, reversing/mixing causal direction.
Unobserved values whose pattern/mechanism can affect inference.
Units cease contributing follow-up data; bias depends on why attrition occurred and its relation to variables/outcomes.
Degree to which comparison groups are sufficiently similar on relevant pre-exposure factors for the intended inference.
Estimated probability of treatment/exposure conditional on observed covariates, usable for specified adjustment/design strategies but unable to control unmeasured confounding by itself.
An exposure/outcome/control chosen because a causal effect is not expected, useful for detecting some biases/confounding under assumptions.
Evidence about whether an exposure precedes an outcome; necessary for many causal claims but insufficient alone.

guards.reason: Concurrent measurement generally cannot establish temporal direction.
Temporal data improve ordering but confounding/reverse pathways can remain.
Case/control counts are selected by outcome status and usually do not represent population prevalence.
Cohort observation does not imply randomized assignment.
Adjustment only addresses modeled/measured variables under assumptions.
Propensity methods balance observed covariates under assumptions and do not remove unmeasured confounding automatically.
Temporal order is important but insufficient for causation.
Missingness mechanism must be investigated/assumed explicitly, not inferred from missingness itself.
Complete-case analysis can be biased depending on missingness/selection.
Natural experiments rely on identification assumptions and external processes, not necessarily literal randomization.
Sample size reduces some sampling uncertainty but does not erase systematic selection, confounding or measurement bias.
Causal interpretation requires an identification strategy and assumptions beyond association.

invariants: Observational methods are legitimate first-class methods, not merely inferior experiments.
Study design determines which quantities/inferences are identifiable.
Cross-sectional association generally lacks temporal ordering.
Longitudinal observation improves temporal information but does not automatically establish causality.
Selection, attrition, missingness, confounding and reverse causation remain explicit risks.
Adjustment methods address only the biases their assumptions/data permit.
Propensity methods do not create literal randomization or solve unmeasured confounding automatically.
Large datasets can have small sampling error and large systematic bias simultaneously.
Observational causal claims retain their identification strategy, assumptions, diagnostics and scope.

provenance.authoring_basis: Core observational epidemiology/social-science design, longitudinal reasoning and quasi/natural-experimental principles adapted to Lantern's causal and methodology architecture.
